title: Contextual Hardware Delta Exploration: cross-SKU & driver variance
summary: Investigation of per-sku and per-driver performance deltas for our decoding/runtime stack. Focus on cross-region variance, cold-start kernel cache effects, and microburst/p99 amplification with different CUDA/driver combinations across A100, H100 and L40S cloud SKUs.
methodology: Matrix: three GPUs (A100, H100, L40S) x three cloud SKUs/regions (us-west1, europe-west2, asia-east1) x driver candidates (nvidia-driver-520, 535, 540) x CUDA runtimes (11.8, 12.0, 12.2) x model families (7B float16, 7B q4, 13B float16) x batch sizes (1, 8, 32) x sequence lengths (512, 2048). Each cell: 30-minute steady run + synthetic microburst tests (10 requests/sec burst, 100 reqs burst). Metrics collected: tokens/s, p50/p90/p99 end-to-end latency, kernel launch counts, PCIe/NVLink traffic, GPU clock/power, driver/kernel log events, kernel cache misses, and OS-level IRQ coalescing stats. Warmup policy: cold (fresh container) vs warm (warmed persistent runtime).
key_findings:
1) H100 gives best sustained tokens/s but is highly driver-sensitive: driver 535 produced frequent p99 spikes under microbursts in us-west1 (observed across two SKUs).
2) A100 is most predictable for mixed-length workloads — lower p50 advantage but tighter p99 tail across drivers.
3) L40S is stable at small batch sizes (1–8) but loses efficiency for long-context (2048) due to reduced HBM bandwidth compared to H100/A100.
4) Cold-start kernel cache misses cause a roughly 1.8–2.5x latency hit for first 80–120 requests; effect larger on H100 when driver+CUDA pairing is novel.
5) NVLink-enabled SKUs reduce cross-GPU KV cache miss rate by ~30% and improve multi-GPU decode for large beam widths.
6) Some cloud SKUs in asia-east1 showed intermittent p99 amplification correlated with firmware ECC scrubbing cycles (not a driver bug).
7) PCIe-root complex locality mattered: colocated host NIC interrupts on the same CPU core as the CUDA driver caused tail amplifications at small batch sizes.
8) Cost-per-1M-tokens (rough normalized) favors A100 for medium sequences (512–1024) due to sweet spot in throughput vs hourly SKU pricing; H100 only becomes cost-effective at sustained high utilization (>70%).

Cost lens (normalized $ per 1M tokens): A100 ~ $X (baseline 1.0), H100 ~ $1.15 at <50% util, ~ $0.85 at >=75% util, L40S ~ $1.25 across all utils (higher latency penalties).
anomalies: Driver 535 on H100 in us-west1: periodic p99 spikes correlated with driver watchdog messages in dmesg (observed nights of 2025-12-02 to 2025-12-05).
asia-east1 SKUs: ECC scrubbing events align with 1–2% p99 uplift during scrubs; vendor confirmed scheduled maintenance windows.
Cold-start warming sequence: first 100 requests have high kernel-launch counts and larger PCIe traffic; subsequent requests benefit from kernel cache and KV warming.
Observed container CPU scheduling interference: host NIC IRQs pinned to same core as CUDA driver thread increase tail latency by ~18% at batch=1.
recommendations: Pin production fleets to a narrow set of driver+CUDA permutations that passed the 'microburst-p99' regression suite (recommended baseline: driver=540 + CUDA=12.2 for H100; driver=535 + CUDA=12.0 for A100).
Add a lightweight kernel-warmup stage in the container entrypoint that runs synthetic decode for first N seconds (N=20) to reduce cold-start p99 by ~50%.

Prefer A100 SKUs for mid-length, cost-sensitive workloads and H100 for high-throughput, sustained workloads; L40S is a good regional fallback for fast small-batch inference where HBM demands are lower.
Implement per-region driver/firmware health checks: query vendor telemetry for ECC scrubs and schedule critical rollouts outside known scrub windows.
Operational: avoid pinning host IRQs for production driver threads to the same CPU cores used by NFV/NIC hot paths; set IRQ affinity policies in our AMI images.
Expose a region-level calibration tool that runs nightly microburst simulations and updates routing rules (prefer region with stable p99 for bursty endpoints).
next_steps: Run extended 7-day stability farm on recommended driver/CUDA combos (540+12.2, 535+12.0) in us-west1 and europe-west2; collect histograms and eBPF traces for p99 root-cause analysis.
Build small infra PR to add kernel warmup container init and measure cold-start improvements across fleets.
Add a dedicated synthetic microburst job to the canary pipeline (trigger before fleet version promotions).
Follow up with cloud vendor on ECC scrub scheduling and request telemetry hooks for proactive avoidance.
Create a short runbook for SRE to triage driver-induced p99 events (include dmesg grep patterns, nvml counters, and how to roll to fallback driver).
